messages:
Maya (partnerships): Quick sync — AxiomAccel reached out to propose a joint performance story (perf/W + throughput) for their T52 tensor ASIC. They want public numbers + a short technical note. We need to lock the bench matrix, kernel variants, telemetry hooks, and an embargo window. @Jordan @Ben @Leo can you weigh in on what's realistic in a 3-week timeline? Evan: can Axiom provide units and firmware baseline?
Jordan (eng-ml): Sounds good. For signal we should include: 1) perf/W (end-to-end), 2) sustained throughput (tokens/s) across batch sizes, 3) p95 token latency, 4) model quality regressions on eval set. Also include int8 vs int4 quant runs.
Ben (eng-runtime): Agree. We'll want to test: - baseline runtime (stock kernels) - flash-attn-v3 enabled - fused-kv-cache + persistent KV path - tuned GEMM kernels for T52. Also need model checkpoints and a deterministic input set. I can draft a runbook.
Leo (eng-infra): Telemetry wise, we need power telemetry at 1s granularity (external PDUs or on-chip counters), per-request token breakdown (time-in-token, kernel-time), and a mechanism to correlate host logs with hw counters. Suggest using our bench-trace pipeline to ingest: 
```
bench.metrics: [throughput, latency_p95, power_w_avg, energy_per_token]
trace_tags: [kernel_variant, quant_mode, batch_size, model_id, firmware_rev]
export: s3://redwood-benching/axiom/t52/{run_ts}/
```
Also add alerts for >10% perf deviation during run.
Asha (cust-success): For the public story we need an embargo date and a single canonical run to quote numbers from. Also confirm data handling — are any customer datasets involved? We should avoid referencing any customers.
Evan (AxiomAccel): We can supply 4 systems in the SF lab (T52 rev1, firmware 1.2.0). Firmware 1.3 has a kernel fix but not stable yet; we can test it in parallel if Redwood wants. We can also provide PDUs for power sampling. Embargo window: we prefer mid-May. Is that feasible?
Maya (partnerships): Mid-May works if we start now. Proposed schedule: week 1 = dry-run (small subset), week 2 = full matrix, week 3 = validation + docs + legal review. Two questions: (1) which models & sizes? (2) who is owner for the bench article?
Jordan (eng-ml): Models: include a small-medium-large sweep to show scaling: redwood-open-7b (small), mixtral-16b (mid), llamaX-70b (large). For quality checks use our standard eval set (common prompts) and log delta-ROUGE/BLEU where applicable. Owner: Jordan for evals, Ben for runtime numbers.
Ben (eng-runtime): I'll own the runbook and kernel toggles. I'll need Axiom firmware images and the exact device kernel ABI. Evan can you share the ABI doc + a sample kernel config? Also request: enable persistent KV path by default for the large runs.
Evan (AxiomAccel): ABI doc sent to Ben via secure link (s3 pre-signed). Firmware 1.2.0 is on the units; 1.3 candidate available on request. We'll also provide a small telemetry agent that exposes per-chip power and temperature at /metrics.
Leo (eng-infra): For ingestion, I'll create a benching dataset and alert rules. Proposed alert: if power variance > 12% across identical runs, fail the run and mark for human triage. Also we should snapshot kernel perf counters with `axiom-prof` before and after the run.
CI Bot: bench-run triggered: run-id=axiom-t52-1955550000-1, owner=ben, matrix=3models x {int8,int4,fp16} x 4batch-sizes.
Maya (partnerships): Nice — action items: 1) Ben draft runbook + kernel matrix by EOD tomorrow. 2) Jordan prepare eval prompt set and pass to Axiom for no-PI check. 3) Evan confirm lab dates (when can you ship units? you said SF lab availability?) 4) Leo spin up bench ingestion + alerting. 5) Asha start draft of partner announcement copy (embargo mid-May). I'll coordinate legal.
Ben (eng-runtime): On it. I'll include command snippets and the exact kernel flags. Example run command I'll start from: 
```bash
./run_bench --model llamaX-70b --quant int8 --kernel flash-attn-v3 --batch 8 --out s3://redwood-benching/axiom/t52/1955550000/llamaX-70b-int8-b8/
```
I'll also capture per-token breakdown and energy per token in the run metadata.
Jordan (eng-ml): I'll share eval set link and a small script to compute delta metrics. Will also add a quality gate: if generation token-level perplexity increases >2% vs baseline, flag the run.
Evan (AxiomAccel): Can do. SF lab can host the machines starting next Tue (1955636400). We'll also provide remote access for Redwood engineers. Firmware 1.2.0 will be preinstalled.
Asha (cust-success): For the announcement, let's not use customer names; focus on raw numbers and a technical appendix. I'll draft the embargoed blog outline.
Maya (partnerships): Great. Quick clarifying Q: are we OK with including int4 results in the public note? Jordan/Ben?
Ben (eng-runtime): Int4 is fine as long as we include accuracy deltas and a clear footnote about quantization toolchain (post-training quant with per-channel scales).
Jordan (eng-ml): Agree. Add a line: "int4 results may require calibration; see appendix."
Leo (eng-infra): One more infra ask: capture ambient lab temp and wall power during runs — that can explain variance. Evan can you share PDU telemetry keys?
Evan (AxiomAccel): PDU keys: axiom-pdu-01..04, endpoint on lab VLAN. I'll send ACL for Redwood infra team.
Maya (partnerships): OK — schedule recap and owners in-thread: Ben (runbook + runs), Jordan (evals + quality gate), Leo (telemetry + alerts), Evan (hardware + firmware + PDUs), Asha (announcement draft), Maya (partnership coordination + legal). Next sync Tue after dry-run results. :calendar:
Ben (eng-runtime): I'll ping once the first dry-run artifacts are uploaded.
Jordan (eng-ml): I'll start the evals this afternoon.
Evan (AxiomAccel): Shipping checklist sent. ETA lab Tue.
Maya (partnerships): Thanks everyone :thumbsup: — closing thread for now, post updates here.
